passages.context: Ross's complete chapter was read in the hashed Book VII HTML alongside the separate Bywater Greek passage. It renders malakia as softness and also uses the historically loaded effeminacy in one explanatory sentence; the Greek record, not this English choice, controls the lexical distinction.
passages.notes: No transcription is registered because the controlling artifact is remote. Ross renders the principal contrast with softness and endurance and later uses the historically loaded effeminacy. His rendering does not establish identity with Thomistic perseverance.

work.author: Aristotle
work.description: Aristotle's ethical treatise in ten books, conventionally addressed by book and chapter and more precisely by Bekker page, column, and line. Book VII distinguishes continence, incontinence, endurance, and softness and tests whether steadfastness follows right reason rather than mere attachment to an opinion.
work.title: Ethica Nicomachea
